statements.text: If a/b = c/d then a, b, c and d are in proportion. Formula: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}$
If a, b, c and d are in proportion, then a/b = c/d. Formula: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}$
The proportion is the equality of two ratios or more.
In the ratio a/b = c/d, a is called the first proportional, b the second proportional, c the third proportional, and d the fourth proportional. Formula: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}$
a and d are called extremes; b and c are called means.
If a/b = c/d then ad = bc (product of the extremes equals product of the means).
If a/b = c/d then a/c = b/d. Formula: $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{b}{d}$
Second: if ad = bc then a/b = c/d and a/c = b/d. Formula: $ad=bc \Rightarrow \frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}, \ \frac{a}{c}=\frac{b}{d}$
First property: if a/b = c/d then a = mc and b = md, where m ∈ R*. Formula: $a=mc, \ b=md, \ m\in\mathbb{R}^*$

Third property: if a/b = c/d = e/f = ..., and m1, m2, m3, ... are in R*, then (a m1 + c m2 + e m3 + ...)/(b m1 + d m2 + f m3 + ...) equals one of the ratios. Formula: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}=\frac{e}{f}=\cdots, \ m_1, m_2, m_3, \ldots\in\mathbb{R}^* \Rightarrow \frac{a m_1+c m_2+e m_3+\cdots}{b m_1+d m_2+f m_3+\cdots}=\text{one of the ratios}$

The quantities a, b and c are in continued proportional if $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{b}{c}$; a is called the first proportional, b the middle proportional, and c the third proportional, where $b^2 = ac$ or $b=\pm\sqrt{ac}$. Formula: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{b}{c}$, $b^2=ac$, $b=\pm\sqrt{ac}$
